The breakdown below covers the recent core framework vulnerability alongside the most common implementation vulnerabilities found in Flask applications.
1. Core Framework Vulnerabilities
Historically, Flask has had very few direct core vulnerabilities. However, a recent major fix occurred in early 2026:
Snyk
The "Vary: Cookie" Cache Leak (CVE-2026-27205):
In
Flask versions 3.1.2 and below
, certain types of session access (such as using the Python
in
operator) failed to trigger the
Vary: Cookie
header. If the app sat behind a caching proxy, sensitive, user-specific data could inadvertently be cached and exposed to other users.
National Institute of Standards and Technology (.gov)
The Fix:
Upgrade to
Flask 3.1.3 or higher
, which natively forces correct cache handling.
